newsitem.title: USA: Soybean prices need to stay high -- Sparks Companies.
newsitem.headline: Soybean prices need to stay high -- Sparks Companies.

text.p: Sparks Companies Inc founder and chairman Willard Sparks said Monday that soybeans have to stay high-priced in order to curb use, build stocks and encourage exports from Latin America.
"The job of the market is to keep these old crop beans high relative to the new crop," Sparks told an agriculture policy conference sponsored by his company.
"This year beans need to stay high, next year they're going to stay relatively lower ... $6.80 a bushel or so," he said.

Sparks also told the group the United States probably needed to shift a few more acres to soybeans. Earlier Monday, the U.S. Agriculture Department pegged 1997 U.S. soybean acreage at 68.8 million acres, the largest since 1980 and above trade expectations.
"We probably still need to shift a few more acres to beans but it's too late this year," Sparks said. He said because of this, Argentina and Brazil soybeans would become more important.
